newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-BAILEY READY TO BREAK OWN WORLD 100 METRES RECORD AGAI.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAILEY READY TO BREAK OWN WORLD 100 METRES RECORD AGAI.

text.p: Canadian Donovan Bailey feels he can break his own world 100 metres record of 9.84 seconds this year, but he will not be attempting it at Sheffield on Sunday.

The 29-year-old Canadian, who set his record when he won the Olympic title last year, will confine himself to a 150 metres race against former Olympic champion Linford Christie of Britain in the Grand Prix meeting at Sheffield.
He reiterated on Friday that he is ready to beat hiw own mark for 100 metres.
"I'm running faster now than I was at this time last year," he told a news conference.

"I weigh around 188-190 pounds compared to 196 last year. I am leaner and stronger and I will improve this year on what I have run previously. I can improve my first 30 metres, my last 30 metres and the middle 40. I'm not even close to running my perfect race yet."

The 150 metres will be Bailey's second race over the hybrid distance in a month following his $1.5 million challenge against American Michael Johnson in Toronto which he won after Johnson pulled up injured.
The prize money at stake on Sunday is a far more modest 50,000 pounds ($80,000).
While Bailey has criticised Christie in the past, on Friday he had nothing but praise for the Briton who has said he will not run in the World Championships in August.
"He is remarkable, at 37, to keep on coming out and doing it year after year.
"I have so much respect for him and I would like to see him run at the World Championship in Athens. He trains hard, he works hard, he is always up for it.
"It wouldn't be my choice to still be running at 37. By the time I am that age I'll probably be playing golf or something."
The Sheffield meeting will be without the other half of the Toronto 150 race - Johnson.
The Olympic and world champion pulled out after finishing fifth in his 400 in Paris on Wednesday in 45.76 seconds, his first defeat over the distance for eight years.

Johnson's manager Brad Hunt and coach Clyde Hart said the defeat was down to "race rustiness" following a three-week layoff after he injured himself in Toronto and that Johnson had returned to the United States.
"He's going home for two weeks," Hunt said. "It isn't an injury, but a matter of fitness."
It means Johnson will have to abandon his attempt at beating the 400 metres world record in Lausanne on Wednesday, although he hopes to race in Stuttgart on July 13.
Another top overseas star missing will be Cuban 800 metres runner Anna Fidelia Quirot, the Olympic silver medallist, who gave no reason for the withdrawal from her race.

Among other top stars competing will be Venuste Niyongabo of Burundi, the Olympic 5,000 metres champion, and 1995 world 100 metres champion Gwen Torrence, the American who will not be defending her title in Athens.
The only real dampener could be the weather with rain that has soaked Britain and washed out much of the Wimbledon tennis likely to continue.
